transcript.text: Good evening, everyone. Let's get started. As we all know, the finale goes live this Saturday at 9:00 PM Eastern, and I'll be making the final binding decision on the voting package. The current draft has SMS and online portal voting open to our broadcast audience. Before I lock anything in, I want to hear from each of you — standards, platform production, rights, and data protection. What issues or concerns do we need to address so we can document the final package and move forward?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a standards issue before we finalize. Per the network's current standards memo — which was issued after the draft voting rules were circulated — there are three binding requirements that the current draft does not yet reflect: voters must be at least 13 years old, each voter may cast exactly one vote per verified account, and voting must close at 9:50 PM Eastern. The draft as it stands doesn't specify an age floor, a one-vote-per-verified-account limit, or a 9:50 PM close. These need to be incorporated into the final package.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical platform issue. I completed the platform certification test this morning, and the SMS integration failed certification — only the web portal passed. The approved portal requires account verification before a vote is accepted. This means SMS voting cannot go forward as currently drafted, and the web portal's account verification requirement needs to be reflected in the final package.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a rights issue. I obtained the finalist label's written approval today. The approval confirms that the voting interface may display finalist names and approved headshots, but it may NOT use any finalist performance audio or video. The current draft interface still contains performance clips, so those must be removed before we finalize the package.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a data protection issue. My privacy review, completed with the voting vendor this week, limits participation to viewers physically located in the United States and Canada, and requires voter identifiers to be deleted within 30 days. The current draft still describes worldwide participation and has no deletion step. Both of these must be corrected in the final package before we lock it in.
